$comment: Single source of truth for the container images and the MCP servers they
carry. Consumed by docker/render.py, which renders venv/servers.tsv (read by
venv/run), the mcpServers block of .claude-plugin/plugin.json, the in-image
server map and the build matrix of .github/workflows/build-images.yml.
Adding a server means editing this file and re-rendering.
Two build strategies, chosen by what the dependency graph allows:
uv          - the image installs one uv project from venv/<venv>/uv.lock,
the same lock a host install uses. A container is then the
same environment with a newer glibc and the build tools
already present, so a command behaves identically in both.
conda-lock  - the generative stack. mattergen hard-pins torch 2.2.1+cu118
wheels that never existed for aarch64, and ADiT/DiffCSP++
are not published packages, so it cannot be a uv project.
Each env is installed side by side from its exact lockfile.

images.name: cpu
images.notes: No torch. Carries every optional extra the architecture allows (openmm, docking; pymol on amd64 only).

images.name: mlip
images.notes: torch 2.10.0: the CUDA 12.8 build on amd64, CUDA 13 on arm64 (GB10). Cannot host fairchem: mace-torch pins e3nn==0.4.4, fairchem-core needs e3nn>=0.5.

images.name: fairchem
images.notes: Same torch as mlip. fairchem-core 2.19.0 declares torch~=2.8.0; the override to 2.10.0 is recorded in venv/fairchem/pyproject.toml.

images.name: generative
images.notes: arm64 only for now. adit/diffcsp/mattergen were assembled by hand -- adit-agent's spec declares only python, pip and uv -- so unlike the uv images their environments cannot be resolved from a spec. torch-scatter/cluster/sparse are compiled from source here. On amd64 these servers need the conda envs under conda-envs/.
